chemistry.questionText: Which of the following alcohols will not undergo oxidation?
chemistry.explanation: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol with no H on the carbinol carbon, so it resists oxidation under normal conditions. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
A voltaic cell is made by connecting two half cells represented by the half equations below:
Sn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Sn(s), E° = −0.14 V
Fe³⁺(aq) + e⁻ → Fe²⁺(aq), E° = +0.77 V
Which statement is correct about this voltaic cell?
chemistry.optionA: Fe²⁺ is oxidised and the voltage of the cell is −0.91 V
chemistry.optionB: Sn is oxidised and the voltage of the cell is 0.91 V
chemistry.optionC: Fe²⁺ is oxidised and the voltage of the cell is 0.91 V
chemistry.optionD: Sn is oxidised and the voltage of the cell is 0.63 V
chemistry.explanation: Sn (lower E°) is oxidised at the anode and Fe³⁺ is reduced. E°cell = 0.77 − (−0.14) = 0.91 V. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Four half reactions I to IV are shown below:
I. 2Cl⁻ → Cl2 + 2e⁻
II. 4OH⁻ → O2 + 2H2O + 4e⁻
III. Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na
IV. 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H2
Which two of these reactions are most likely to occur when concentrated brine is electrolysed?
chemistry.explanation: In concentrated brine, Cl⁻ is oxidised to Cl2 at the anode (I) and water/H⁺ is reduced to H2 at the cathode (IV); Na is not formed. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which property of transition metals enables them to behave as catalysts?
chemistry.explanation: Transition metals act as catalysts because of their variable oxidation states (and ability to adsorb reactants). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024, 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: In the two tetrahedral structures of the dichromate ion:
chemistry.optionA: 4 Cr – O bonds are equivalent in length.
chemistry.optionB: 6 Cr – O bonds are equivalent in length.
chemistry.optionC: All Cr – O bonds are equivalent in length.
chemistry.explanation: Dichromate has two CrO4 tetrahedra sharing one oxygen. The six terminal Cr–O bonds are equivalent; the two bridging Cr–O–Cr bonds are longer. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: 1 mole of liquid A and 2 moles of liquid B make a solution having a total vapour pressure 40 torr. The vapour pressure of pure A and pure B are 45 torr and 30 torr respectively. The above solution
chemistry.explanation: Ideal pressure = (1/3)(45) + (2/3)(30) = 35 torr. The observed 40 torr is higher, so the solution shows positive deviation. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following would not be a good choice for reducing nitrobenzene to aniline?
chemistry.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces aromatic nitro compounds to azo compounds, not aniline. Sn/HCl, Fe/HCl and H2/Ni give aniline. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: If molality of a dilute solution is doubled, the value of the molal elevation constant (Kb) will be
chemistry.explanation: Kb is a property of the solvent only, so it does not change with molality. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Hydrolysis of sucrose is called
chemistry.explanation: Hydrolysis of sucrose changes the optical rotation from dextro to laevo, so it is called inversion and the product invert sugar. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which one of the following has lowest pKa value?
chemistry.explanation: –NO2 has a stronger −I effect than –Cl, so nitroacetic acid is the strongest acid, with the lowest pKa. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following cell was used in Apollo space programme?
chemistry.explanation: H2–O2 fuel cells were used to provide electrical power (and drinking water) in the Apollo space programme. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Proteins are polymers of α-amino acids connected by peptide bonds.
Reason (R): A tetrapeptide contains 4 amino acids linked by 4 peptide bonds.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: proteins are polymers of α-amino acids joined by peptide bonds. The reason is false: a tetrapeptide has 4 amino acids linked by 3 peptide bonds. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): For a zero order reaction the unit of rate constant and rate of reaction are same.
Reason (R): Rate of reaction for zero order reaction is independent of concentration of reactant.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: rate = k[R]⁰ = k, since rate is independent of concentration, so rate and k have the same units. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): trans-[CrCl2(ox)2]³⁻ shows optical isomerism.
Reason (R): Optical isomerism is common in octahedral complexes involving didentate ligands.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is false: the trans form has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive; only cis-[CrCl2(ox)2]³⁻ is optically active. The reason is true. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Consider the following standard electrode potential values:
Fe³⁺(aq) + e⁻ → Fe²⁺(aq), E° = +0.77 V
MnO4⁻(aq) + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺(aq) + 4H2O(l), E° = +1.51 V
What is the cell potential for the redox reaction between MnO4⁻ and Fe²⁺?
chemistry.explanation: MnO4⁻ (higher E°) is reduced at the cathode and Fe²⁺ is oxidised. E°cell = 1.51 − 0.77 = +0.74 V. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The magnetic moment of [NiCl4]²⁻ is: [Atomic number: Ni = 28]
chemistry.explanation: Ni²⁺ (3d⁸) in tetrahedral [NiCl4]²⁻ (weak-field Cl⁻) has 2 unpaired electrons: μ = √(n(n+2)) = √8 ≈ 2.82 BM. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following ions has the electronic configuration 3d⁶? (Atomic numbers: Mn = 25, Co = 27, Ni = 28)
chemistry.explanation: Co (3d⁷4s²) loses three electrons to give Co³⁺: 3d⁶. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following aqueous solution will have highest boiling point?
chemistry.explanation: ΔTb ∝ i·m: KCl 1 M = 2, K2SO4 1 M = 3, KCl 2 M = 4, K2SO4 2 M = 6. The 2.0 M K2SO4 solution boils highest. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Amides can be converted into amines by the reaction named
chemistry.explanation: Amides are converted to primary amines with one carbon fewer by Hoffmann bromamide degradation (Br2/NaOH). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following statements is not true about glucose?
chemistry.optionB: On heating with HI it forms n-hexane.
chemistry.optionC: It is present in pyranose form.
chemistry.explanation: Glucose does not give the 2,4-DNP test (nor Schiff's test), indicating the –CHO group is not free — it exists in the cyclic (pyranose) form. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024, 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Vitamin C cannot be stored in our body.
Reason (R): Vitamin C is fat soluble and is excreted from the body in urine.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: vitamin C cannot be stored in the body. The reason is false: vitamin C is water-soluble (not fat-soluble), so it is regularly excreted in urine. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The half life of a reaction is the time in which the concentration of the reactant is reduced to one half of its initial concentration.
Reason (R): In first order kinetics when concentration of reactant is doubled, its half life is doubled.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: it is the definition of half-life. The reason is false: for first-order kinetics, t½ = 0.693/k is independent of initial concentration. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Bromination of benzoic acid gives m-bromobenzoic acid.
Reason (R): Carboxyl group increases the electron density at the meta position.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: –COOH is meta-directing. The reason is false: –COOH withdraws electrons and decreases electron density, most strongly at the ortho and para positions, so meta is relatively richer. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Consider the following standard electrode potential values:
Sn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Sn(s), E° = −0.14 V
Fe³⁺(aq) + e⁻ → Fe²⁺(aq), E° = +0.77 V
What is the cell reaction and potential for the spontaneous reaction that occurs?
chemistry.explanation: The spontaneous reaction has positive E°: 2Fe³⁺ + Sn → 2Fe²⁺ + Sn²⁺, E° = 0.77 − (−0.14) = +0.91 V. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The unit of molar conductivity is
chemistry.explanation: Λm = κ/c, giving units S cm² mol⁻¹. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Out of the following 1.0 M aqueous solutions, which one will show largest freezing point depression?
chemistry.explanation: ΔTf ∝ i. Al2(SO4)3 gives 5 ions (i = 5), the largest among these. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: In the reaction C6H5NH2 + CHCl3 + 3KOH → A + 3B + 3C, the product A is:
chemistry.explanation: A primary amine with CHCl3 and alcoholic KOH gives an isocyanide (carbylamine): C6H5NH2 → C6H5NC (+3KCl + 3H2O). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: β-pleated sheet structure in proteins refers to:
chemistry.explanation: The α-helix and β-pleated sheet are secondary structures of proteins. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The backbone of DNA and RNA molecules is a chain consisting of heterocyclic base, pentose sugar and phosphate group.
Reason (R): Nucleotides and nucleosides mainly differ from each other in the presence of a phosphate group.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is false: the backbone is an alternating sugar-phosphate chain, with bases attached as side groups. The reason is true: a nucleotide is a nucleoside plus a phosphate group. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): [Co(NH3)5SO4]Cl gives a white precipitate with silver nitrate solution.
Reason (R): The complex dissociates to give Cl⁻ and SO4²⁻ ions.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: [Co(NH3)5SO4]Cl gives Cl⁻, which precipitates as white AgCl. The reason is false: SO4²⁻ is coordinated to Co, so the complex gives only [Co(NH3)5SO4]⁺ and Cl⁻. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2024, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Choose the compound which is more acidic than phenol:
chemistry.explanation: An electron-withdrawing –NO2 group makes o-nitrophenol more acidic than phenol. Ethanol and phenols with donor groups (–CH3, –OCH3) are less acidic. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
A reaction follows second order kinetics. How is the rate of reaction affected if the concentration of the reactant is reduced to half ?
Choose the correct value from the following:
chemistry.explanation: For second order, rate ∝ [A]². Halving [A] makes the rate 1/4 of the original. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Solutions of two electrolytes X and Y are diluted. Molar conductivity of X increases 25 times whereas that of Y increases 1·5 times. Which one is a stronger electrolyte?
chemistry.explanation: Strong electrolytes show only a small increase in Λm on dilution, so Y (1.5 times) is the strong one. X (25 times) is weak. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Unit of rate constant for the zero order reaction is:
chemistry.explanation: For a zero-order reaction, rate = k, so k has units mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which type of isomerism is shown by the complexes [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 and [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br?
chemistry.explanation: Exchange of the ligand (Br⁻/SO4²⁻) with the counter-ion is ionisation isomerism. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: What would be the major product of the reaction of methanal (HCHO) with CH3MgI followed by hydrolysis (H2O)?
chemistry.explanation: HCHO + CH3MgI followed by hydrolysis gives a primary alcohol with one more carbon: ethanol. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The oxidation state of the central metal atom in the complex [Co(NH3)4(H2O)2]Cl3 is:
chemistry.explanation: NH3 and H2O are neutral and the complex ion carries +3 (balanced by 3Cl⁻), so Co is +3. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Phenol gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol on treatment with concentrated HNO3 and concentrated H2SO4.
Reason (R): OH group in phenol is m-directing.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: phenol with concentrated HNO3/H2SO4 gives picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol). The reason is false: –OH is ortho/para-directing. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
The rate law for a particular reaction is given as rate = k[A][B]2. How is the rate of reaction affected if we double the concentration of B ?
Choose the correct option:
chemistry.explanation: Rate ∝ [B]², so doubling [B] makes the rate four times. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: A galvanic cell can behave as an electrolytic cell when:
chemistry.explanation: If an external voltage greater than Ecell is applied in the opposite direction, the current reverses and the galvanic cell works as an electrolytic cell. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023, 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Three compounds are given below : C2H5NH2 , (C2H5)2NH, (C2H5)3N I II III The correct decreasing order of their basic strength in an aqueous solution is:
chemistry.explanation: In aqueous solution, basicity of ethylamines is (C2H5)2NH > (C2H5)3N > C2H5NH2, due to a balance of inductive effect, solvation and steric factors. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which type of isomerism is exhibited by the given complex ? [Pt(NH3)2Cl2]
chemistry.explanation: Square planar [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] exists as cis and trans forms (geometrical isomerism). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: A reaction is first order in A and second order in B. How is the rate affected when the concentrations of both A and B are doubled?
chemistry.explanation: Rate = k[A][B]². Doubling both gives 2 × 4 = 8 times. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which type of isomerism is shown by the complex [Co(en)3]³⁺?
chemistry.explanation: [Co(en)3]³⁺ is chiral (it has no plane of symmetry), so it shows optical isomerism. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The most common oxidation state for all lanthanoids is:
chemistry.explanation: +3 is the most common oxidation state of all lanthanoids. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2023)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water?
chemistry.explanation: ΔTf ∝ i·m. At equal molarity, CaCl2 (i = 3) gives the lowest freezing point. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following is not a transition metal?
chemistry.explanation: Hg (like Zn and Cd) has a completely filled d¹⁰ configuration in its ground state and common oxidation state, so it is not regarded as a transition metal. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than Ea?
chemistry.explanation: The fraction of molecules with energy ≥ Ea is given by the Boltzmann factor e^(−Ea/RT). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: What will happen during the electrolysis of aqueous solution of CuCl2 by using platinum electrodes?
chemistry.optionB: H2 gas will be released at cathode
chemistry.optionC: O2 gas will be released at anode
chemistry.optionD: Cl2 gas will be released at anode
chemistry.explanation: In aqueous CuCl2 with Pt electrodes, Cu deposits at the cathode and Cl2 is released at the anode. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of
chemistry.explanation: Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, made by acetylating salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The secondary valency of Co in the complex [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]²⁺ is:
chemistry.explanation: Five NH3 and one NO2⁻ give coordination number (secondary valency) 6. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dil. HNO3 to yield
chemistry.explanation: Dilute HNO3 at low temperature gives a mixture of ortho- and para-nitrophenols. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Aniline on direct nitration yields
chemistry.explanation: In strongly acidic medium aniline becomes the anilinium ion (meta-directing), so direct nitration gives about 51% para, 47% meta and 2% ortho products. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness:
chemistry.explanation: Deficiency of vitamin E causes increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation.
Reason (R): Components of an azeotrope have the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: an azeotrope has the same composition in liquid and vapour phases and boils at a constant temperature, so fractional distillation cannot separate it. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The presence of –OH group in phenols directs the incoming group to the meta position in the ring.
Reason (R): –OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is false: –OH is ortho/para-directing. The reason is true: –OH activates the ring. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with H2N–OH.
Reason (R): It indicates the presence of a free –CHO group in glucose.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine. The reason is false: this indicates the absence of a free –CHO group (glucose exists in cyclic form). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following is most basic?
chemistry.explanation: The basic character of oxides decreases with oxidation state; MnO (+2) is the most basic, while Mn2O7 is acidic. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following solutions will have the highest osmotic pressure?
chemistry.explanation: π = iCRT. At equal concentration, CaCl2 (i = 3) gives the highest osmotic pressure. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: For the reaction N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, the rate of reaction with respect to NH3 is:
chemistry.explanation: For N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, rate = +(1/2)Δ[NH3]/Δt. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: How many faradays are required to reduce 1 mol of Cr2O7²⁻ to Cr³⁺ in acidic medium?
chemistry.explanation: Cr2O7²⁻ → 2Cr³⁺: each Cr goes from +6 to +3, i.e. 6 electrons, so 6 faradays. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The secondary valency of Pt in [Pt(en)2Cl2]²⁺ is:
chemistry.explanation: Two didentate en and two Cl⁻ give coordination number (secondary valency) 6. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: (CH3)3C – OC2H5 on reaction with HI gives
chemistry.explanation: With a tertiary alkyl group the reaction follows SN1: the stable tert-butyl carbocation forms, giving (CH3)3C–I and C2H5–OH. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: An example of non-reducing sugar is
chemistry.explanation: In sucrose the reducing groups of glucose and fructose are involved in the glycosidic bond, so it is a non-reducing sugar. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The two strands of DNA are complementary to each other.
Reason (R): The hydrogen bonds are formed between specific pairs of bases.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: specific base pairing (A–T, G–C) through hydrogen bonds makes the two strands complementary. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following is the correct expression of Kf, which depends upon the nature of the solvent?
chemistry.explanation: Kf = R × M1 × Tf² / (1000 × ΔfusH), which depends only on the solvent (molar mass, freezing point and enthalpy of fusion). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following transition metals has lowest enthalpy of atomisation?
chemistry.explanation: Mn (3d⁵4s²) has a stable half-filled d subshell, weak metallic bonding and so the lowest enthalpy of atomisation among these. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The secondary valency of Co in [Co(en)3]3+ is
chemistry.explanation: Three didentate en ligands give 3 × 2 = 6 donor atoms, so the secondary valency is 6. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: At low temperature, phenol on reaction with Br2 in CS2 gives
chemistry.explanation: In a non-polar solvent (CS2) at low temperature, phenol gives a mixture of o- and p-bromophenols. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: How the conductivity varies on decreasing concentration for both weak and strong electrolytes?
chemistry.optionA: It increases for weak electrolyte and decreases for strong electrolyte.
chemistry.optionB: It decreases for weak electrolyte and increases for strong electrolyte.
chemistry.optionC: It increases for both weak and strong electrolytes.
chemistry.optionD: It decreases for both weak and strong electrolytes.
chemistry.explanation: Conductivity (κ) decreases on dilution for both weak and strong electrolytes because the number of ions per unit volume decreases. Molar conductivity increases. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: CH3 – NH2 on reaction with (CH3CO)2O gives
chemistry.explanation: Acetylation of methylamine gives N-methylacetamide, CH3–NH–CO–CH3. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The activation energy of a reaction can be determined from the slope of which of the following curves?
chemistry.explanation: ln k = ln A − Ea/RT, so a plot of ln k vs 1/T is a straight line with slope −Ea/R. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Identify 'X' in the following reaction:
CH3–CO–CH2–CO–O–CH3 —(NaBH4)→ 'X'
chemistry.explanation: NaBH4 reduces the ketone group but not the ester, giving CH3–CH(OH)–CH2–CO–OCH3. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Actinoids show irregularities in their electronic configurations.
Reason (R): Due to varying stabilities of f0, f7 and f14 occupancies of the 5f orbitals.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: the irregular configurations arise from the extra stability of f⁰, f⁷ and f¹⁴ occupancies. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Consider the following reaction:
Zn(s) + Ag2O(s) + H2O(l) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s) + 2OH⁻(aq)
Given: E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = 0.80 V, E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, 1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹
ΔrG° for the above reaction is:

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Identify the correct statement:
chemistry.optionA: Molecularity of a reaction is an experimental quantity.
chemistry.optionB: For complex reactions molecularity has no meaning.
chemistry.optionC: Molecularity of a reaction can be zero or even a fraction.
chemistry.optionD: Molecularity more than three is very common in chemical reactions.
chemistry.explanation: Molecularity applies only to elementary reactions; for complex reactions it has no meaning. It is theoretical, never zero or fractional, and rarely above three. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The order for the reaction A + 2B → Products, with Rate = k[A]^(1/2)[B]¹, is:
chemistry.explanation: Order = sum of exponents in the rate law = 1/2 + 1 = 1.5. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Electronic configuration of chromium is:
chemistry.explanation: Cr (Z = 24) is [Ar] 3d⁵4s¹ because the half-filled d subshell is extra stable. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The correct IUPAC name of the complex [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] is:
chemistry.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine before chlorido) and Pt is +2: diamminedichloridoplatinum(II). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following is heteroleptic complex?
chemistry.explanation: A heteroleptic complex has more than one kind of ligand. [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ has NH3 and Cl⁻. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following molecules is chiral in nature?
chemistry.explanation: Butan-2-ol has a carbon bearing four different groups (H, OH, CH3, C2H5), so it is chiral. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Identify the correct increasing order of boiling points of the given compounds:
chemistry.explanation: Boiling point increases with molar mass and decreases with branching: propan-1-ol < butan-2-ol < butan-1-ol < pentan-1-ol. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Identify the compound produced by the reduction of Ethanenitrile with Lithium aluminium hydride:
chemistry.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces CH3–C≡N to CH3CH2NH2 (ethylamine). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The base which is present in DNA but not in RNA is:
chemistry.explanation: Thymine is present in DNA, while RNA has uracil in its place. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Proteins are polymers of α-amino acids which are joined to each other by:
chemistry.explanation: α-Amino acids in proteins are joined by peptide (–CO–NH–) bonds. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Glucose gets oxidized to six carbon gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
Reason (R): The carbonyl group is absent in the open chain structure of glucose.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is true: bromine water oxidises glucose to gluconic acid. The reason is false: the open-chain structure has a carbonyl (–CHO) group, which is what gets oxidised. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following reactions is not explained by the open chain structure of glucose?
chemistry.optionA: Glucose on prolonged heating with HI forms n-hexane.
chemistry.optionB: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.
chemistry.optionC: Glucose gets oxidized to gluconic acid on reaction with bromine water.
chemistry.optionD: Glucose exists in two different crystalline forms, alpha (α) and beta (β).
chemistry.explanation: The existence of α and β anomers can be explained only by the cyclic structure. The other reactions are explained by the open-chain structure. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The intermediate formed during the slowest step involved in the dehydration of alcohol is:
chemistry.explanation: In acid-catalysed dehydration, the slow (rate-determining) step is loss of water from the protonated alcohol, forming a carbocation. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The oxidation number of Co in [Co(en)3]2(SO4)3 is:
chemistry.explanation: Two complex cations balance three SO4²⁻, so each [Co(en)3] carries +3. Since en is neutral, Co is +3. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: According to Werner’s theory, the primary valencies of the central metal atom:
chemistry.optionA: are satisfied by neutral molecules or negative ions.
chemistry.optionB: are equal to its coordination number.
chemistry.explanation: Primary valencies are ionisable and are satisfied by negative ions; secondary valency equals the coordination number. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following reagent is used to distinguish between (C2H5)2NH and (C2H5)3N?
chemistry.explanation: Benzenesulphonyl chloride reacts with secondary amines (giving an alkali-insoluble sulphonamide) but not with tertiary amines. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: In aqueous solution, Cr2O7²⁻ ion converts to which of the following in alkaline medium?
chemistry.explanation: In alkaline medium dichromate converts to chromate: Cr2O7²⁻ + 2OH⁻ → 2CrO4²⁻ + H2O. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The boiling point of an azeotropic mixture of water and ethanol is less than that of pure water and ethanol. The mixture shows:
chemistry.optionD: that the solution is an ideal solution.
chemistry.explanation: A minimum-boiling azeotrope (like ethanol–water) has a higher vapour pressure than expected, so it shows positive deviation from Raoult's law. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Separation of Zr and Hf is difficult.
Reason (R): Because Zr and Hf lie in the same group of the periodic table.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: Zr and Hf are hard to separate because lanthanoid contraction gives them almost identical radii and properties. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The oxidation number of Co in [Co(NH3)5 (ONO)] SO4 is:
chemistry.explanation: The complex ion is +2 (balancing SO4²⁻); NH3 is neutral and ONO⁻ is −1, so Co = +3. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which reagent is used to distinguish between C2H5NH2 and (C2H5)2NH?
chemistry.explanation: Only primary amines give the carbylamine (isocyanide) test with CHCl3 and ethanolic KOH, so it distinguishes C2H5NH2 from (C2H5)2NH. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: In aqueous acidified solution, CrO4²⁻ ion converts to which of the following?
chemistry.explanation: In acidic solution chromate converts to dichromate: 2CrO4²⁻ + 2H⁺ → Cr2O7²⁻ + H2O. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The boiling point of an azeotropic mixture of water and nitric acid is more than that of pure water and nitric acid. The mixture shows:
chemistry.optionB: that solution is an ideal solution
chemistry.explanation: A maximum-boiling azeotrope (like HNO3–water) shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: For the reaction 2A → 3B, the rate of reaction +d[B]/dt is equal to:
chemistry.explanation: Rate = −(1/2) d[A]/dt = +(1/3) d[B]/dt, so d[B]/dt = −(3/2) d[A]/dt. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Order of reaction is not applicable for elementary reaction but applicable for complex reaction.
Reason (R): Order of reaction is an experimental quantity.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is false: order applies to both elementary and complex reactions (molecularity has no meaning for complex reactions). The reason is true. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The oxidation number of Pt in [Pt(en)2Cl2]2+ is:
chemistry.explanation: en is neutral and Cl⁻ is −1: x − 2 = +2, so Pt is +4. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which reagent is used to distinguish between primary, secondary and tertiary amines?
chemistry.explanation: Hinsberg's reagent, C6H5SO2Cl, distinguishes primary, secondary and tertiary amines. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The correct order of decreasing basic strength in aqueous solution of the following is:
chemistry.explanation: In water, ethylamines' basicity is (C2H5)2NH > (C2H5)3N > C2H5NH2, due to a combined inductive, solvation and steric effect. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Consider the following compounds : Chlorobenzene (I), 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene (II), 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (III), 4-nitrochlorobenzene (IV) The correct order of increasing ease of nucleophilic substitution reactions of these compounds is:
chemistry.explanation: Electron-withdrawing –NO2 groups at o/p positions activate the ring towards nucleophilic substitution; more –NO2 groups make it easier. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The half-life periods of decomposition of NH3 for different initial pressures are given below : p (torr) 704 75 34·5 t1/2 (min) 80 80 80 The order of the reaction is:
chemistry.explanation: t½ stays the same at different initial pressures, which is characteristic of a first-order reaction. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Ethers have lower boiling points than the boiling points of alcohols.
Reason (R): This is due to the presence of hydrogen bonding in alcohols.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: alcohols are associated by intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which ethers lack. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Oxidation of chloroform by air in the presence of sunlight produces a poisonous gas known as:
chemistry.explanation: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air in light to the poisonous gas phosgene (COCl2), so it is stored in dark bottles. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Lucas reagent produces cloudiness immediately with:
chemistry.explanation: Tertiary alcohols, like 2-methyl-2-propanol, give turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + ZnCl2). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following d-orbitals experience more repulsion in the crystal field splitting of octahedral complex?
chemistry.explanation: In an octahedral field, the eg orbitals (dx²−y², dz²) point directly at the ligands and face more repulsion. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The chelating ligand used for the treatment of lead poisoning is:
chemistry.explanation: EDTA is used to treat lead poisoning by forming a stable chelate with Pb²⁺. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Manganate ion is paramagnetic due to the presence of:
chemistry.explanation: In MnO4²⁻ manganese is +6 (3d¹), with one unpaired electron, so it is paramagnetic. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: When a liquid and its vapour are at equilibrium and the pressure is suddenly decreased:
chemistry.optionA: vapour pressure of the solution increases
chemistry.explanation: When pressure drops, more liquid evaporates to restore equilibrium; evaporation absorbs heat, so cooling occurs. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Nucleic acids are polymers of:
chemistry.explanation: Nucleic acids are polynucleotides — polymers of nucleotides. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Alcohols act as Bronsted bases as well as Bronsted acids.
Reason (R): It is due to the presence of unshared electron pairs on oxygen atom and presence of polar O – H bond.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: lone pairs on oxygen accept protons (base), and the polar O–H bond releases protons (acid). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): E°(Sc³⁺/Sc²⁺) has a low value.
Reason (R): Because of the stability of Sc³⁺ ion which has a noble gas configuration.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: Sc³⁺ has a stable noble-gas configuration, so reducing Sc³⁺ to Sc²⁺ is unfavourable and E° is low. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which property of transition metals enables them to form alloys?
chemistry.explanation: Transition metals have similar atomic radii, so one metal atom can readily replace another in the lattice, forming alloys. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Williamson synthesis is an example of:
chemistry.explanation: In Williamson synthesis an alkoxide ion attacks an alkyl halide by SN2, a nucleophilic substitution. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Number of possible stereoisomers for the complex [Co(en)2Cl2]Cl will be:
chemistry.explanation: [Co(en)2Cl2]⁺ has a trans form (optically inactive) and a cis form that exists as two enantiomers, giving 3 stereoisomers. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The correct order of decreasing basic strength of CH3 − NH2, (CH3)2NH and (CH3)3N in aqueous solution is:
chemistry.explanation: In water, methylamines' basicity is (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following reagent is used to convert benzene diazonium chloride to benzene?
chemistry.explanation: Ethanol (or H3PO2) reduces benzenediazonium chloride to benzene. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following is not correct for SN1 reaction?
chemistry.optionC: Proceeds through the formation of carbocation
chemistry.explanation: SN1 goes through a planar carbocation, so it gives racemisation, not inversion. Inversion is characteristic of SN2. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The coordination number of Co in [Co(en)2Cl2]+ is:
chemistry.explanation: Two didentate en (4 donor atoms) and two Cl⁻ give a coordination number of 6. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The correct order of decreasing order of pKb values is:
chemistry.explanation: Higher pKb means a weaker base. Aniline is the weakest, N-methylaniline is slightly stronger, and ethylamine is the strongest: C6H5NH2 > C6H5NHCH3 > C2H5NH2. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Each polypeptide in a protein has amino acids linked with each other in a specific sequence and it is this sequence of amino acids that is said to be:
chemistry.explanation: The specific sequence of amino acids in a polypeptide is the primary structure of the protein. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the reactions is used in the conversion of a ketone into hydrocarbon?
chemistry.explanation: Wolff–Kishner reduction (NH2NH2, then KOH/ethylene glycol) converts C=O to CH2. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Which of the following reagents are used to prepare primary amines by Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction?
(i) R–CO–NH2  (ii) NaOH  (iii) Br2  (iv) CHCl3
chemistry.explanation: An amide (i) with Br2 (iii) and NaOH (ii) gives a primary amine with one carbon fewer. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The major product of carbylamine reaction is:
chemistry.explanation: Primary amines heated with CHCl3 and alcoholic KOH give foul-smelling isocyanides. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Actinoids show larger number of oxidation states:
chemistry.optionA: because they are radioactive in nature
chemistry.optionB: because they have large atomic numbers
chemistry.optionC: because they have large atomic masses
chemistry.optionD: due to comparable energies of 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals
chemistry.explanation: The 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals have comparable energies, so actinoids show a larger number of oxidation states. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Consider the following reaction and identify A and B:
CH3Cl + NaI —(dry acetone)→ A + B
chemistry.explanation: CH3Cl + NaI in dry acetone gives CH3I and NaCl. NaCl precipitates, driving the reaction forward. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The correct formula of Hinsberg’s reagent is:
chemistry.explanation: Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride, C6H5SO2Cl. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Half-life (t1/2) of a first order reaction is 1386 s. The value of rate constant is:
chemistry.explanation: k = 0.693/t½ = 0.693/1386 s = 5.0 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following ligands forms a chelate complex?
chemistry.explanation: Oxalate (C2O4²⁻) is a didentate ligand, so it forms a chelate ring. NH3, H2O and NO2⁻ are monodentate. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols can be distinguished by:
chemistry.explanation: The Lucas test (conc. HCl + ZnCl2) separates 1°, 2° and 3° alcohols by how quickly turbidity appears. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Consider the following compounds : C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C6H5CH2NH2, NH3, C6H5NH2 The correct increasing order of the above compounds on the basis of their basic strength is:
chemistry.explanation: Aryl amines are weakest; benzylamine behaves like an alkylamine; and in water 2° > 1°: C6H5NH2 < NH3 < C6H5CH2NH2 < C2H5NH2 < (C2H5)2NH. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Identify the polysaccharide among the following:
chemistry.explanation: Cellulose is a polysaccharide of β-D-glucose units. Glucose and fructose are monosaccharides; maltose is a disaccharide. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): p-nitrophenol is more acidic than phenol.
Reason (R): Nitro group is an electron-withdrawing group, it stabilises phenoxide ion by dispersal of negative charge.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: –NO2 withdraws electrons and stabilises the p-nitrophenoxide ion. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
In an electrochemical cell, the following reaction takes place:
2Cu⁺(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Cu(s) + Zn²⁺(aq), Ecell = 1.28 V
As the reaction progresses, what will happen to the overall voltage of the cell?
chemistry.explanation: Ecell = E°cell − (0.059/2) log([Zn²⁺]/[Cu⁺]²). As [Zn²⁺] rises and [Cu⁺] falls, Ecell decreases. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Out of Fe³⁺, Sc³⁺, Cr³⁺ and Co³⁺ ions, the one which is colourless in aqueous solution is: [Atomic number: Fe = 26, Sc = 21, Cr = 24, Co = 27]
chemistry.explanation: Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰, so no d–d transition is possible and it is colourless. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction is given by:
chemistry.explanation: Hoffmann bromamide degradation is given by amides: ArCONH2 + Br2 + NaOH → ArNH2. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The value of Henry’s constant KH is:
chemistry.optionA: greater for gases with higher solubility
chemistry.optionB: greater for gases with lower solubility
chemistry.optionD: not related to the solubility of gases
chemistry.explanation: p = KH·x, so for a given pressure a larger KH means a smaller mole fraction, i.e. lower solubility. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Out of the following statements, the incorrect statement is:
chemistry.optionA: La is actually an element of transition series.
chemistry.optionB: Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii because of lanthanoid contraction.
chemistry.optionC: Ionic radius decreases from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺ ion.
chemistry.explanation: Lanthanoids in general are not radioactive (only promethium is), so D is incorrect. The other statements are correct. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Out of 2-Bromobutane, 1-Bromobutane, 2-Bromopropane and 1-Bromopropane, the molecule which is chiral in nature is:
chemistry.explanation: 2-Bromobutane has a chiral carbon (H, Br, CH3, C2H5). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The product of the oxidation of I⁻ with MnO4⁻ in alkaline medium is:
chemistry.explanation: In alkaline (or neutral) medium, MnO4⁻ oxidises iodide to iodate: 2MnO4⁻ + I⁻ + H2O → 2MnO2 + 2OH⁻ + IO3⁻. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Polyhalogen compounds have wide application in industries and agriculture. DDT is also a very important polyhalogen compound. It is a:
chemistry.explanation: DDT is an insecticide that is not biodegradable, so it accumulates in food chains. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: What amount of electric charge is required for the reduction of 1 mole of MnO4⁻ into Mn²⁺?
chemistry.explanation: MnO4⁻ (Mn +7) → Mn²⁺ (+2) needs 5 electrons per ion, so 5F per mole. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Alkenes are formed by heating alcohols with conc. H2SO4. The first step in the reaction is:
chemistry.explanation: The first step in acid-catalysed dehydration is protonation of the alcohol to form an oxonium ion. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Out of Ti³⁺, Cr³⁺, Mn²⁺ and Ni²⁺ ions, the one which has the highest magnetic moment is: [Atomic number: Ti = 22, Cr = 24, Mn = 25, Ni = 28]
chemistry.explanation: Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) has 5 unpaired electrons, the most among these (Ti³⁺ 1, Cr³⁺ 3, Ni²⁺ 2), so its magnetic moment is highest. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Out of Ti³⁺, Cr³⁺, Fe²⁺ and Ni²⁺ ions, the one which is the most stable ion in aqueous solution is: [Atomic number: Ti = 22, Cr = 24, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
chemistry.explanation: Cr³⁺ (3d³, half-filled t2g) is the most stable in aqueous solution; Ti³⁺ and Fe²⁺ are easily oxidised. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Out of the following statements, the correct statement is:
chemistry.optionA: La is actually not an element of transition series.
chemistry.optionB: Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii.
chemistry.optionD: Ionic radius increases from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺.
chemistry.explanation: Because of lanthanoid contraction, Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii. Ionic radius decreases (not increases) from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺, and lanthanoids in general are not radioactive. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: What amount of electric charge is required for the oxidation of 1 mole of FeO to Fe2O3?
chemistry.explanation: Fe goes from +2 in FeO to +3 in Fe2O3, losing 1 electron per Fe, so 1F per mole of FeO. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The role of a catalyst is to change:
chemistry.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative path with lower activation energy. It does not change ΔH, ΔG or the equilibrium constant. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2024, 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following molecules is chiral in nature?
chemistry.explanation: 2-Chlorobutane has a chiral carbon (H, Cl, CH3, C2H5). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: CH3CH2OH can be converted to CH3CHO by:
chemistry.explanation: PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) oxidises primary alcohols to aldehydes without further oxidation to acids. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The IUPAC name for CH3 – CH2 – N(CH3) – CH2 – CH2 – CH3 is:
chemistry.explanation: The longest chain on N is propyl, with ethyl and methyl as N-substituents: N-ethyl-N-methylpropan-1-amine. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The treatment of ethyl bromide with alcoholic silver nitrite gives:
chemistry.explanation: AgNO2 is mainly covalent and attacks through nitrogen, so ethyl bromide gives nitroethane (C2H5NO2). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following aqueous solutions will have the highest freezing point?
chemistry.explanation: ΔTf ∝ i. Glucose does not dissociate (i = 1), so it has the smallest depression and the highest freezing point. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following aldehydes will undergo Cannizzaro reaction?
chemistry.explanation: Only aldehydes without α-hydrogen undergo the Cannizzaro reaction; (CH3)3C–CHO has none. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
In which of the following groups are both ions coloured in aqueous solution?
I. Cu⁺  II. Ti⁴⁺  III. Co²⁺  IV. Fe²⁺
[Atomic number: Cu = 29, Ti = 22, Co = 27, Fe = 26]
chemistry.explanation: Co²⁺ (3d⁷) and Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) have unpaired d electrons and are coloured. Cu⁺ (3d¹⁰) and Ti⁴⁺ (3d⁰) are colourless. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: CH3CH2CHO and CH3CH2COOH can be distinguished by:
chemistry.explanation: Propanoic acid gives brisk effervescence of CO2 with NaHCO3; propanal does not. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Match the type of cell given in Column I with their use given in Column II.
Column I Column II i. Lead storage cell a. Wall clock ii. Mercury cell b. Apollo Space Programme iii. Dry cell c. Wrist watch iv. Fuel cell d. Inverter
chemistry.explanation: Lead storage cell → inverter, mercury cell → wrist watch, dry cell → wall clock, fuel cell → Apollo space programme. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): For measuring resistance of an ionic solution an AC source is used.
Reason (R): Concentration of ionic solution will change if DC source is used.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: DC would cause electrolysis and change the solution's concentration, so AC is used. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Henry’s law constant (KH) decreases with increase in temperature.
Reason (R): As the temperature increases, solubility of gases in liquids decreases.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: The assertion is false: KH increases with temperature. The reason is true: gas solubility decreases as temperature rises (which is why KH increases). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2024, 2025, 2026)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The solubility of aldehydes and ketones in water decreases with increase in size of the alkyl group.
Reason (R): Aldehydes and ketones have dipole-dipole interaction.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: solubility falls because the larger hydrophobic alkyl group hinders hydrogen bonding with water. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The boiling points of alkyl halides decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
Reason (R): The van der Waals forces of attraction decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: larger, more polarisable halogens give stronger van der Waals forces and higher boiling points. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: While doing qualitative analysis in chemistry lab, Abhishek added yellow coloured potassium chromate solution into a test tube. He was surprised to see the colour of the solution changing immediately to orange. He realised that the test tube was not clean and contained a few drops of some liquid. Which of the following substances will be the most likely liquid to be present in the test tube before adding potassium chromate solution?
chemistry.explanation: Yellow chromate turns orange dichromate in acid: 2CrO4²⁻ + 2H⁺ → Cr2O7²⁻ + H2O. So the tube contained HCl. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Williamson synthesis of preparing unsymmetrical ether is:
chemistry.explanation: Williamson synthesis is an SN2 attack of an alkoxide ion on a primary alkyl halide. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following compounds would be hydrolysed by aqueous KOH most easily?
chemistry.explanation: Allyl bromide is hydrolysed most easily because the allylic carbocation/transition state is resonance-stabilised. Vinyl bromide is least reactive. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: According to Werner’s theory of coordination compounds:
chemistry.optionC: Both primary and secondary valences are non-ionisable.
chemistry.optionD: Both primary and secondary valences are ionisable.
chemistry.explanation: Primary valences are ionisable; secondary valences are non-ionisable. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following complex ion is not optically active?
chemistry.explanation: trans-[Co(en)2Cl2]⁺ has a plane of symmetry, so it is optically inactive. The others are chiral. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following is the softest metal?
chemistry.explanation: Zn (3d¹⁰4s²) has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding, so it is soft with low melting point. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: In the Hinsberg’s method for separation of primary, secondary and tertiary amines, the reagent used is:
chemistry.explanation: Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride, C6H5SO2Cl. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which one of the following amines gives an alcohol on reaction with HNO2?
chemistry.explanation: Primary aliphatic amines give alcohols with HNO2 (evolving N2): C2H5NH2 → C2H5OH. Aniline gives a diazonium salt. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The freezing point of one molal KCl solution, assuming KCl to be completely dissociated in water, is : (Kf for water = 1·86 K kg mol–1)
chemistry.explanation: ΔTf = i·Kf·m = 2 × 1.86 × 1 = 3.72 K, so the freezing point is −3.72 °C. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: A solution of acetone in ethanol:
chemistry.optionC: shows a positive deviation from Raoult’s law.
chemistry.optionD: shows a negative deviation from Raoult’s law.
chemistry.explanation: Acetone breaks the hydrogen bonds between ethanol molecules, weakening interactions, so the solution shows positive deviation. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following cell converts the energy of combustion of fuel into electrical energy?
chemistry.explanation: Fuel cells convert the energy of combustion of fuels (H2, CH4, etc.) directly into electrical energy. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The unit of rate and rate constant are same for a:
chemistry.explanation: For zero order, rate = k, so rate and k have the same units (mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Pyranose ring of glucose is formed due to the reaction between:
chemistry.explanation: The –OH at C5 reacts with the –CHO at C1 to form a six-membered hemiacetal (pyranose) ring. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Hydrolysis of an ester follows first order kinetics.
Reason (R): The concentration of water does not get altered much during the reaction.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: water is in large excess and its concentration hardly changes, so acidic hydrolysis of an ester is (pseudo) first order. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which by-product is obtained in the manufacture of phenol from cumene?
chemistry.explanation: Cumene hydroperoxide on acid treatment gives phenol and acetone (by-product). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which reagents are required for one step conversion of chlorobenzene to toluene?
chemistry.explanation: Chlorobenzene + CH3Cl + Na in dry ether gives toluene (Wurtz–Fittig reaction). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The coordination number of Fe in [Fe(C2O4)3]³⁻ is:
chemistry.explanation: Three didentate oxalate ligands give 6 donor atoms, so the coordination number is 6. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following complexes shows geometrical isomerism?
chemistry.explanation: [MA4B2]-type octahedral [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ exists as cis and trans isomers. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The reagent that can be used to convert benzenediazonium chloride to benzene is:
chemistry.explanation: Mild reducing agents like ethanol (or H3PO2) replace –N2⁺Cl⁻ with H, giving benzene. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The gas evolved when methylamine reacts with HNO2 is:
chemistry.explanation: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO2 to evolve N2 gas quantitatively (and form alcohols). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The value of rate constant for a pseudo first order reaction:
chemistry.optionB: depends on the concentration of reactants present in small amount.
chemistry.optionC: depends on the concentration of reactants present in large excess.
chemistry.optionD: is not dependent on the concentration of reactants.
chemistry.explanation: For a pseudo first-order reaction, k' = k[B], where B is the reactant in large excess, so it depends on that concentration. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Boiling point of (C2H5)2NH is lower than that of n-C4H9NH2.
Reason (R): Hydrogen bonding is much more extensive in n-C4H9NH2 as compared to (C2H5)2NH.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: a primary amine has two N–H hydrogens for hydrogen bonding, while a secondary amine has one. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: During dehydration of alcohol to alkene by heating with conc. H2SO4, the initiation step is:
chemistry.explanation: The first step is protonation of the alcohol by acid to form a protonated alcohol (oxonium ion). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which reagents are required for one step conversion of Chlorobenzene to Diphenyl?
chemistry.explanation: Two molecules of chlorobenzene with Na in dry ether couple to give diphenyl (Fittig reaction). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following complexes show linkage isomerism?
chemistry.explanation: The ambidentate NO2⁻ ligand can bind through N (nitro) or O (nitrito), so [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]²⁺ shows linkage isomerism. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following transition metals has the highest melting point?
chemistry.explanation: Cr has the maximum number of unpaired d electrons (3d⁵4s¹), giving strong metallic bonding and the highest melting point among these. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The strongest base in aqueous solution among the following amines is:
chemistry.explanation: In water, (C2H5)2NH is the strongest base among ethylamines; aniline is the weakest. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: On mixing 30 mL of acetone with 20 mL of chloroform, the total volume of solution is:
chemistry.explanation: Acetone and chloroform form hydrogen bonds (negative deviation), so ΔVmix < 0 and the total volume is less than 50 mL. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: We cannot measure the resistance of an ionic solution using DC because:
chemistry.optionA: it changes the composition of the solution.
chemistry.optionB: it can cause sparks and shocks.
chemistry.optionC: it does not affect the composition of the solution.
chemistry.optionD: it converts electrolytic cell to galvanic cell.
chemistry.explanation: DC causes electrolysis, which changes the composition of the solution, so AC is used. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The primary and secondary valences of Co in [Co(en)3]Cl3 respectively are:
chemistry.explanation: Primary valence = 3 (three ionisable Cl⁻). Secondary valence = coordination number = 6 (three didentate en). (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: In the Arrhenius equation k = A·e^(−Ea/RT), 'A' represents:
chemistry.explanation: A is the pre-exponential (frequency) factor. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction.
Reason (R): Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: actinoid contraction is greater because 5f electrons shield the nuclear charge poorly. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): The bond angle C – O – C in ethers is slightly greater than tetrahedral angle.
Reason (R): This is because of the repulsive interaction between the two bulky alkyl groups.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
chemistry.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
chemistry.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
chemistry.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: repulsion between bulky alkyl groups widens the C–O–C angle slightly above 109°28'. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following transition metal ion is not coloured?
chemistry.explanation: Cu⁺ is 3d¹⁰ with no unpaired electrons, so no d–d transition — colourless. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following solutions will have the highest boiling point in water?
chemistry.explanation: ΔTb ∝ i × (moles per gram). CaCl2: 3/111 = 0.0270; KCl: 2/74.5 = 0.0268; urea: 1/60; glucose: 1/180. CaCl2 is highest. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: During electrolysis of dilute H2SO4, using platinum electrodes, the gas evolved at the anode is:
chemistry.explanation: In dilute H2SO4, water is oxidised at the anode to give O2. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The number of moles of AgCl precipitated when excess AgNO3 solution is mixed with one mole of [Co(NH3)3Cl3] is:
chemistry.explanation: In [Co(NH3)3Cl3] all three Cl⁻ are coordinated and the complex is neutral, so no AgCl precipitates. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: Which of the following haloalkanes react with aqueous KOH most rapidly by SN1 reaction?
chemistry.explanation: 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane forms a stable tertiary carbocation, so it reacts fastest by SN1. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: The reaction 2R–OH + 2Na → 2RO⁻Na⁺ + H2(g) suggests that alcohols are:
chemistry.explanation: Reaction with Na to liberate H2 shows that alcohols can donate a proton, i.e. are acidic. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: At low temperature, phenol reacts with Br2 in CS2 to form:
chemistry.explanation: In CS2 at low temperature, monobromination gives a mixture of o- and p-bromophenols. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: When alkyl iodide is treated with large excess of ammonia, the major product obtained is:
chemistry.explanation: With a large excess of ammonia, the alkyl halide reacts mainly with NH3, so the primary amine is the major product. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: An amine ‘X’ reacts with Hinsberg reagent and the product obtained is soluble in alkali. The amine ‘X’ is:
chemistry.explanation: Primary amines give an N-alkylsulphonamide with an acidic N–H, which dissolves in alkali. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText: α-Helix structure refers to:
chemistry.explanation: The α-helix (like the β-pleated sheet) is a secondary structure of proteins. (CBSE Class 12 Chemistry 2025)

chemistry.subject: Chemistry
chemistry.questionText:
Assertion (A): A mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol can be separated by steam distillation.
Reason (R): o-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
chemistry.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
